[Original LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7513831629178486784/)

This past weekend my team placed 2nd at UBC in the National Health Datathon 2026 led by UofT's Temerty Centre for AI Research and Education in Medicine (T-CAIREM). I really enjoyed working with a group of talented individuals from across health and data-related disciplines.

Our work explored whether biopsy slides can help predict how breast cancer patients respond to pre-surgery therapy. Working with whole-slide images from about 100 patients, we preprocessed the images and extracted embeddings using Phikon, a pathology foundation model. We then reduced those feature embeddings using PCA and combined them with cancer subtype in a logistic regression model to predict pathological complete response. In our experiments, adding image features improved on a baseline that used cancer subtype alone.

My own focus was on whole-slide image processing and extracting embeddings from the foundation model, where I built one of the two pipelines our team developed in parallel. I was impressed with how much a pretrained foundation model let us do with so little data.

The work was done on confidential clinical data in a secure environment so the data and code unfortunately can't be shared.

A big thank you to UBC Data Science and Health (DASH) for hosting the UBC site and to my teammates Vincent Luong, Joseph Lenczowski, April Lee, Daegan Sit, and  Muse Park.

I look forward to participating in more events like this in the future!
